outcome.answer:
For synthetic data curation for LLM training, two key approaches are: (1) curating synthetic datasets using group-level signals rather than only per-sample utility, and (2) doing data curation online via reweighting during training.

“Effective Synthetic Data Curation Requires Group-Level Signals” argues that individual-level estimates of training utility are insufficient because different synthetic dataset compositions can look similar under individual influence but differ sharply when samples’ interactions are considered; it proposes group-level estimation for better downstream generative performance and gives a cheaper diagnostic to prioritize which groups need group-level estimation [1]. “Rethinking Data Curation in LLM Training…” (ADAPT) instead replaces offline filtering/mixing with online per-sample loss weighting guided by similarity-based quality signals, dynamically acting like an implicit curriculum and improving generalization under equal FLOPs [3].

If your focus is synthetic data generation/validation rather than curation for training, “LLM as a Meta-Judge” uses controlled semantic degradation to create synthetic evaluation datasets that proxy human metric validation [5], and “AutoSynth” automates workflow discovery for synthetic dataset generation using LLM-as-judge reward components without labeled reward-model data [4].
